articles.title: Deebo Samuel cleared for Week 10
articles.summary: The 49ers' versatile wide receiver is set to play in Week 10.
articles.body:
San Francisco 49ers WR Deebo Samuel (hamstring) practiced fully on Friday, Nov. 13, and no longer appears on the injury report for Week 10 against the Dallas Cowboys.

Why It Matters: Samuel being in the 49ers' lineup could make him the WR1 in the offense in Week 10. Fantasy players could have him in their flex spot against a soft Cowboys defense.

articles.title: Mets rumors: Ken Rosenthal questions New York being favorite for Tarik Skubal narrative
articles.summary: Tarik Skubal is the big fish in the MLB free agency pond, as nearly every team is going to attempt to sign the two-time Cy Young Award winner. The New York M...
articles.body:
Tarik Skubal is the big fish in the MLB free agency pond, as nearly every team is going to attempt to sign the two-time Cy Young Award winner. The New York Mets have been deemed the favorites to potentially sign Skubal, however, insider Ken Rosenthal isn't buying the buzz in the rumor mill.

During the latest episode of "Foul Territory," Rosenthal admitted that he simply doesn't believe the Mets are truly the favorites to sign the soon-to-be 30-year-old left-hander. But Rosenthal also won't rule out owner Steven Cohen to get the signing done either.

"I know there's a feeling out there among a lot of people that the Mets are the favorites [to sign Skubal]; I'm not sure, and it remains to be seen," Rosenthal said. "All it takes is one snap of Steve Cohen's fingers to make this happen for the Mets. David Stearns, in general, has not loved long-term deals for starting pitchers. But at this point, Stearns might not have the choice."

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

Tarik Skubal is linked to numerous organizations in the rumor mill, including the Mets, Los Angeles Dodgers, San Diego Padres, and Toronto Blue Jays, amongst others. The seven-year veteran will certainly have a bidding war before ultimately choosing where to sign.

Skubal finished last season playing 16 games for the Detroit Tigers and 10 for the Dodgers. While his play didn't earn him his third Cy Young Award (he missed nearly two months of playing time), the two-time All-Star still finished with an impressive 2.72 ERA and 0.964 WHIP with 186 strikeouts through 158.2 innings pitched.

articles.title: Harold Fannin Jr. on track to play in Week 10
articles.summary: Browns TE Harold Fannin Jr. was upgraded to full practice Friday and will be ready to play
articles.body:
Cleveland Browns TE Harold Fannin Jr. (groin) fully participated in practice Friday, Nov. 13, and is not on the injury report for Week 10.

Why It Matters: Fannin missed some practice time during the week but should be able to handle his normal workload in Week 10. He is one of the main options in the Browns passing game and can be considered a low-end No. 1 tight end in leagues.

articles.title: Raiders Week 10 fantasy start/sit: Brock Bowers in, Ashton Jeanty sits
articles.summary: Brock Bowers stays locked in, but Fernando Mendoza's first start and a stout Seattle defense push Ashton Jeanty and the rookie QB to the bench.
articles.body:
For Week 10, the biggest fantasy story in Las Vegas has nothing to do with a running back. Kirk Cousins is in Minnesota , Fernando Mendoza is the starter, and every Raiders skill player's outlook shifted the moment that trade went through. Here's how I'd handle the key pieces against Seattle.

Mendoza's only NFL action came late in a Week 5 loss to the New England Patriots, when he went 6 of 8 for 48 yards . Now he gets a Seattle Seahawks defense that allows an NFL-low 244.2 yards per game in his first start.

I love the long-term upside of a Heisman winner who completed 72% of his passes for 3,535 yards at Indiana last season. In one-quarterback leagues, though, I'm not starting a rookie in this spot, and even superflex managers should treat him as a low-end QB2.

Bowers has drawn 70 targets in seven games , roughly 10 every time he plays. Young quarterbacks tend to lean on the most reliable target on the field, and nobody on this roster fits that description better.

Even in a tough matchup, that kind of volume keeps him in my lineup. He's a TE1 whoever takes the snaps, and if Mendoza feels pressure, Bowers is the outlet I'd bet on him finding.

The Raiders' ground game ranks second-worst in the league at 71.3 rushing yards per game , and Seattle hasn't allowed a 100-yard rusher in 38 straight games, playoffs included. Neither number points to a breakout.

Jeanty's 42 catches give him a little PPR floor, but last week showed me how thin that floor can get. I'd leave him on the bench in standard leagues and use him only as a desperation flex in PPR.

Tucker has 33 catches and averages roughly 16 yards per grab, so his weeks depend on hitting a big play or two. Deep timing between a receiver and a rookie in his first start is usually the last thing to come together.

I'd wait a week or two to see how Mendoza spreads the ball before trusting Tucker in a lineup again.

Here is my sneaky play for deep leagues and two-tight end formats. Michael Mayer has 39 catches for 388 yards, and a rookie quarterback who needs short, easy completions could look his way often.

He won't win anybody a week by himself. But if you need a TE2 or a deep-league flex, though, Mayer's role looks steadier than most of what is sitting on the waiver wire.

articles.title: Washington football among teams impacted by FAA ground stoppage
articles.summary: The Washington Huskies are among several college football teams that have been impacted by Friday's FAA ground stoppage.
articles.body:
This post will be updated with new information as it is received.

Ahead of a matchup with Michigan State, the Washington Huskies are among a handful of teams in college football that have been impacted by an FAA equipment outage that has issued a ground stoppage for all flights traveling across the United States on Friday.

"The directive instructs all departing aircraft to remain on the ground until further notice," USA TODAY reported on Friday afternoon. "Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said the ground stop followed a communication issue affecting all Air Route Traffic Control Centers."

All planes that are currently in the air will be allowed to land at their destinations, and according to the Seattle Times' Andy Yamashita, Washington's plane barely missed the cutoff window before the stoppage was issued. A Washington spokesperson has since stated that the Huskies have left Boeing Field and returned to campus, where they will await a further update.

As of 3:00 p.m. PT, the FAA's website reads that the ground stoppage at Seattle-Tacoma International Airport and Boeing Field, where the Huskies fly out of, is planned until 5:00 p.m. PT. However, that is subject to change before Washington's matchup with the Spartans , which is scheduled for 4:15 p.m. ET/1:15 p.m. PT on Saturday afternoon.

According to a report from ESPN's Pete Thamel, the Huskies are one of three Big Ten teams affected by the outage, along with Minnesota and Purdue; however, the Boilermakers will reportedly take buses to Iowa. Washington does not have that same luxury.

It's unclear whether the Big Ten will offer any alternatives.

articles.title: Delaware Academy removed from Section 4 football final over player eligibility; Middletown drops appeal ahead of Section 9 final
articles.summary: Thursday night, Delaware Academy announced that it had been forced to forfeit its Section 4 Class D semifinal win over Deposit/Hancock from this past weekend...
articles.body:
Another sectional football championship game in New York State has been thrown into chaos as a result of a ruling over player eligibility.

Meanwhile, a team that was previously forced to forfeit its spot in a championship game has dropped its appeal after heading to court seeking emergency relief to have its berth in a title game restored.

Thursday night, Delaware Academy announced that it had been forced to forfeit its Section 4 Class D semifinal win over Deposit/Hancock from this past weekend, removing the state's No. 2-ranked Class D team from its spot in a sectional final this weekend.

In a letter posted to the district's Facebook page , Delaware Academy Central School District at Delhi Superintendent Carey Shultz wrote that Section 4 had ruled the Bulldogs must forfeit their semifinal win and the remainder of their 2026 season "due to a sectional eligibility rule we were unaware of."

In the letter, Shultz said that the ruling came in the wake of a similar issue that occurred elsewhere in the state. Earlier this week, the Middletown football team was forced to forfeit its semifinal win in the Section 9 Class AA playoffs and removed from its spot in a sectional championship game after using an ineligible player.

"Prompted by recent news from another school within New York State, the district was reviewing its readiness for the upcoming sectional final when we learned our team would not be able to advance," Shultz wrote. "Section IV's ruling is based on its eligibility requirements for teams entering sectional play."

Under state rules, football players must be considered an eligible participant for a minimum of three regular season games to be eligible for postseason competition

Delaware Academy had a 9-1 record following its 49-14 semifinal win over Deposit/Hancock and had been scheduled to play Tioga in the sectional final. In his letter, Shultz noted that the Delaware Academy district has filed an appeal of Section 4's decision and that the championship game has been pushed back to Sunday "to allow time for the appeal to be reviewed."

In a follow-up letter posted Friday afternoon on the district's Facebook page, Shultz wrote that Section 4 upheld its original decision, but noted that the district "is in the process of pursuing future remedies," and has requested assistance through state Sen. Peter Oberacker's office while also making an additional appeal through the New York State Public High School Athletic Association.

Meanwhile, according to reports from multiple media outlets , the Enlarged City School District of Middletown withdrew its petition to get its spot in Saturday's Section 9 Class AA championship game against Newburgh Free Academy restored following a hearing Friday in state Supreme Court in Orange County.

The Middie Bears had a perfect 10-0 record after their 48-15 semifinal victory over Valley Central this past weekend, but were removed from the postseason earlier this week when they were forced to forfeit that game due to using an ineligible player.

According to court documents, the unnamed player in question was a member of the Middletown boys' soccer program who joined the football program as a kickoff specialist late in the season. The player appeared in one regular-season game and was listed as an eligible participant - but was not in uniform - for another, then appeared in the sectional semifinal.

The Middletown district, which referred to the issue as an "unintentional adult error in understanding the rules" in a letter posted to the district website, had a waiver request denied by Section 9 and an appeal denied by NYSPHSAA. Local officials weighed in with letters of support, and a Change.org petition started in support of the Middletown team had nearly 6,500 signatures as of late Friday morning.

On Wednesday, the district filed a petition in state Supreme Court in Orange County seeking emergency relief. The hearing was held Friday before Judge Verris B. Shako.

NYSPHSAA, in its response to the petition, noted that Middletown athletic director Justin Sturge was in attendance at a mandatory workshop for Section 9 athletic directors earlier this year where the rule "was clearly explained," and that a Monroe County court upheld the rule in a similar case in 2014 when Aquinas Institute was forced to forfeit its spot in the Section 5 postseason when a quarterback who had only participated in two games prior to sectional playoffs was ruled ineligible.

Valley Central and Newburgh Free Academy are now set to play for the Section 9 Class AA championship on Saturday at noon at Monroe-Woodbury final. The Section 9 champion will play the Section 2 Class AA champion - either Saratoga Springs or CBA - in the regional playoffs next week.

A third sectional championship game that had been in doubt, the Section 5 Class B game between Honeoye Falls-Lima and East/World of Inquiry School, will proceed as scheduled on Saturday despite prior concerns that East/World of Inquiry would be forced to forfeit in the wake of a bench-clearing incident after the final whistle of its semifinal win over James Monroe.

Section 5 officials announced Wednesday that, following an investigation by the Rochester City School District and a review by both Section 5 and NYSPHSAA, multiple East/WOIS players "were misidentified as a disqualified player." East/WOIS will face Honeoye Falls-Lima for the sectional title on Saturday at 3 p.m. at St. John Fisher University.

articles.title: Indiana Pacers got good news on forward Aaron Nesmith vs. New York Knicks
articles.summary: Pacers forward Aaron Nesmith was originally listed as questionable for Friday's game but Indiana got good news ahead of game vs Knicks
articles.body:
INDIANAPOLIS -- Forward Aaron Nesmith will be available for the Indiana Pacers' game against the New York Knicks , the team announced ahead of the game on social media.

Nesmith was previously listed as questionable for Friday's game after he left Wednesday's win over the Washington Wizards with right knee soreness. When asked pregame on Friday if Nesmith would play, head coach Rick Carlisle said "hope so."

Nesmith played 22 minutes on Wednesday, scoring just two points on 1-of-6 shooting. It was his lowest-scoring game of the season so far.

T.J. McConnell, who was listed as probable, will also be available for the Pacers on Friday night. Tyrese Haliburton (hamstring), Johnny Furphy (ACL tear), and Ben Sheppard (meniscus) remain out.

articles.title: Nets' Nolan Traore (calf soreness) probable Saturday at Grizzlies
articles.summary: Here is the full injury report for the Brooklyn Nets heading into Saturday's matchup at the Memphis Grizzlies.
articles.body:
The Brooklyn Nets (3-8) are coming off their most impressive win of the season after beating the New Orleans Pelicans on Wednesday 145-111 thanks to how well they played on both ends of the floor. Brooklyn was understandably happy with themselves after the victory, especially given the issues they've been working through this season, but they will have to keep focusing on the bigger picture in the meantime.

The Nets announced on Friday that second-year guard Nolan Traore is probable for Saturday's matchup at the Memphis Grizzlies due to right calf soreness. Traore missed Wednesday's victory over the Pelicans due to the ailment, but given that he is listed as probable, it seems that he's likely to only miss one game with the calf soreness that he has been feeling lately.

Moving on with the injury report, the Nets also listed rookie guard Mikel Brown Jr. as questionable for Saturday's game in Memphis as he continues to work his way through an illness. While Traore is likely to be back in the rotation, if Brown is unable to take the floor, head coach Jordi Fernandez will still have to figure out how to make up for the point guard minutes that would normally go to the former Louisville Cardinal.

With Traore and Brown unavailable for Wednesday's win at the Pelicans, Egor Demin was the starting point guard with players like Terance Mann and Keon Ellis seeing time as the backups to Demin. More to the point, forwards Julius Randle and Danny Wolf took turns initiating the offense, a feature of Fernandez's offensive scheme in that most of the players essentially share the role of making plays for others.

Some good news for the Nets is they will have the rest advantage over the Grizzlies given that they play against the Pelicans on Friday before facing Brooklyn less than 24 hours later. Heading into their matchup against New Orleans, Memphis will not have center Zach Edey, guard Scotty Pippen Jr., or center Quinten Post so there is a chance that the Nets could face a compromised Grizzlies team as well.

articles.title: College Football Teams Caught Up in Nationwide Flight Stoppage
articles.summary: Three Big Ten teams are still trying to travel to game sites.
articles.body:
The Federal Aviation Administration grounded all flights in the United States on Friday until further notice "due to extraordinary circumstances and for reasons of safety," citing a "temporary communications outage."

With no timeline for planes to get back in the air, numerous college football teams with games scheduled for Saturday are in limbo, waiting for the nationwide ground stop to lift so they can travel for away games.

The Big Ten conference confirmed to Front Office Sports that Minnesota, Purdue, and Washington are all affected. Michigan is scheduled to play at Penn State, Purdue at Iowa, and Washington at Michigan State. All other road teams are grounded at their locations.

The ACC confirmed to FOS that all football teams are at their respective sites for Saturday's games. But Oregon State at Boise State, the site of this week's ESPN's College Gameday , is affected as Oregon State has yet to depart to Boise . ESPN did not immediately respond to an FOS request for comment.

College football isn't the only sport affected. The University of Southern California women's basketball team announced via X that they are grounded in Los Angeles; the team is scheduled to play South Carolina on Sunday in Greenville, South Carolina.

Aviation tracker FlightAware projects thousands of flights within and out of the United States are currently affected. Athletic conferences are still determining the most efficient way to proceed.

"We are in the process of gathering information from all athletic teams since we have several sports competing on the road this weekend," the Mountain West conference told FOS.

The last nationwide ground stop was in January 2023, when a pilot notification system went down. Prior to that, a nationwide ground stop was issued after the September 11 attacks in 2001, prompting postponements across college athletics and professional sports leagues.
